task: Write docs/PLAN.md: a comprehensive, clean-room build plan for David's own Loom clone that integrates the best ideas from nine researched recorders
prompt:
You are the plan writer for David's own Loom-style recorder. Work in /Users/dave/Work/loom-clone (the repo root). Write or improve exactly one file: docs/PLAN.md. Do not edit anything else.

Inputs, read all of them first:
- docs/process/reader-brief.md (product context and clean-room rules)
- docs/research/*.md and docs/research/*.json (nine clean-room research notes; the JSON has per-area presence and quality 0-5, and ranked best_ideas with ids and reuse modes)
- tools/checks/sources.json (repos, pinned SHAs, licences, licence classes, permissive sub-paths)

Clean-room boundary. You are on the BUILD side. You may open the permissive clones under ~/Work/reference-repos/loom (class permissive in sources.json: Screendrop, better-shot, voom, OpenScreen, Kap, Bloom) and the permissive sub-paths of copyleft clones (Cap: crates/camera*, crates/scap-*, vendor/; Recordly: services/recordly-share) to confirm details. Never open any other file in CapSoftware__Cap, webadderallorg__Recordly or alyssaxuu__screenity. Also never open the files listed under copyleft_paths in sources.json: better-shot is BSD-3 overall but 4 of its files are AGPL (adapted from Cap) and 3 are GPLv3 (adapted from MacShot). Read each source's caution_paths note (Screendrop/RecordingViewportTimeline.swift has an unresolved provenance question) and carry it into the plan's Clean-room rules and Risks. Everything you know about the copyleft parts comes from the research notes.

What the plan must decide and explain:
- Base strategy, with the options compared and one recommendation tied to evidence in the notes: fork or build on Screendrop (CC0, Swift, macOS), build fresh in Swift reusing permissive parts, start from OpenScreen (MIT, Electron/TypeScript plus Rust compositor), or a Tauri/Rust app reusing Cap's MIT camera and screen-capture crates.
- macOS first. Screen, camera, microphone and optional system audio recorded as separately editable files with a shared clock, so David's own editor can take a screen file plus a camera file plus an offset.
- Loom-style speed: fast start, camera bubble, stop-to-share-link quickly. Local-first storage; optional share links on storage David controls (for example Cloudflare R2 or any S3-compatible bucket) with a simple viewer page.
- Agent-drivable: a CLI or JSON interface so an AI agent can start, stop, export and share.
- Integrate, do not list: for each feature area pick the best source by the notes' quality scores and evidence, resolve conflicts between ideas, and say what we build ourselves.

Required structure, using these exact ## headings in this order: Summary; Product scope (MVP, later, out of scope); Feature matrix; Architecture; Recording pipeline; Project format; Editing and export; Transcription and AI; Sharing and viewer; Roadmap; Clean-room rules for the build; Open decisions; Risks; Sources and licences; Ideas considered.
- Feature matrix: a table with columns | Area | Phase | Best source | Licence | Reuse mode | Approach |, one row per feature area id from sources.json, the id in backticks in the Area cell. Reuse mode is one of copy-with-notice, clean-room, idea-only, own-design. copy-with-notice is allowed only from permissive repos; for Cap or Recordly it is allowed only when the Best source cell cites a backticked permissive path (for example a crates/scap-* folder).
- Architecture: compare the stack options in a short table, recommend one, then name the modules, the process model, and the platform APIs.
- Project format: the on-disk layout of one recording and its metadata, as a short schema you design yourself.
- Roadmap: at least four ### Phase N subsections. Each has its scope and a 'Done when' list of observable checks (a command, a file, a measured number), not vague wishes.
- Clean-room rules for the build: what build sessions may and may not open (including copyleft_paths inside permissive repos), how attribution notices are kept for copied permissive code (a NOTICE or THIRD_PARTY file), and how to handle a feature only a copyleft repo has.
- Open decisions: at least three real decisions for David, each with options and your recommended default.
- Sources and licences: one entry per repo (all nine slugs), its licence, what we take, how (reuse mode), and the attribution duty.
- Ideas considered: every best_ideas id from docs/research/*.json, each marked adopt, defer or reject with a one-line reason and the phase if adopted.

Writing rules: plain, literal sentences, one idea per sentence, define a term the first time it appears. Fenced code blocks only for our own schemas or interfaces, at most 40 lines each. Never paste text from the reference repos.

Each pass after the first: read the failed-verifier findings given to you, fix those first, then strengthen the weakest section.

Before you finish, run both checks yourself and fix until they pass:
- python3 -I tools/checks/check_plan.py   (must print OK)
- python3 -I tools/checks/check_clean.py docs   (first line must be 0)
The third check is an independent reviewer from a different model family scoring the plan on buildability, faithfulness to the notes, integration, fit to David's needs, licence correctness and decision quality. Do not commit; the host commits after verification. Never weaken, skip or game a check; if you cannot meet the bar honestly, say so in your result notes.
done_when: check_plan.py exits 0 (prints OK), check_clean.py docs reports 0 copyleft overlaps, and an independent Kimi K3 reviewer scores the plan >= 9/10

verify.rubric: Read /Users/dave/Work/loom-clone/docs/PLAN.md, docs/research/*.json and docs/process/reader-brief.md in that repo. Grade the plan 0-10 and give the score of its WORST dimension: (1) buildability: an engineer who has never seen the reference repos could start Phase 1 tomorrow from it (concrete modules, platform APIs, file formats, order of work); (2) faithfulness: what the plan says each reference repo does matches the research notes, and the best source picked for each area is justified by the notes' quality scores and evidence; (3) integration: one coherent product, conflicts between ideas resolved, not a list of repos; (4) fit to David's needs in the reader brief's product context: macOS first, separate screen, camera and mic files with a shared clock for his editor, local-first, self-hosted share links, agent-drivable; (5) licence correctness: copy-with-notice only from permissive sources or permissive sub-paths, attribution duties stated, build-side rules clear; (6) decision quality: open decisions are real with options and a recommended default, and every roadmap phase has observable done-when checks. 9 or above means you would hand it to a build team as is.

assumptions: Working project name loom-clone; David can rename it.
macOS first; other platforms are a later decision recorded under Open decisions.
The plan writer is a Claude Opus subagent that reads only clean-room notes and permissive clones; the rubric checker is Kimi K3 (different family), run read-only via tools/checks/score_kimi.py.
